story_type: fisherman overboard at night far offshore, crew recovers him, swimmer rides the hoist to a pitching deck
hook: He fell overboard 160 miles out at 3:30 in the morning.
narration: He went over the side of a fishing boat one hundred and sixty miles east of Boston.
It was about three thirty in the morning, in November.
His crewmates on the seventy-two foot Jennifer Anne got him back aboard and called the Coast Guard.
A Jayhawk helicopter and an Ocean Sentry plane launched from Air Station Cape Cod.
Over a fishing boat, masts and rigging can snag a hoist cable. So the rescue swimmer rides the cable down, and the flight mechanic lowers him onto open deck.
[short pause] The boat kept pitching under him the whole way down.
outcome: The Jayhawk crew hoisted the fisherman aboard a little over three hours after the call.
title: Overboard 160 miles out at 3:30 a.m.
description:
On Nov. 19, 2020, a Coast Guard Air Station Cape Cod MH-60 Jayhawk crew hoisted a fisherman who had fallen overboard from the 72-foot fishing vessel Jennifer Anne, 160 miles east of Boston, after his crewmates got him back aboard.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Air Station Cape Cod, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/773353/coast-guard-medevacs-man-160-miles-east-boston

facts.source_quote: The Coast Guard medevaced an injured fisherman 160 miles east of Boston, Thursday.
At approximately 3:30 a.m., Coast Guard District One watchstanders received a notification
reporting a 35-year-old crewmember had fallen overboard and was recovered by the other crew members.
